definition: The practice of dividing a dataset into separate subsets for training a model and evaluating its performance on unseen data.
details: A proper train-test split (often supplemented with a validation set) is essential for producing an honest estimate of how well a model will generalize to new, unseen data.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Train-Test Split — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
